### Raw-output spot check (5 random rows)

Seed-42 sample of 5 rows from the 3,200 downloaded sampled replies (8 of 26 contexts pulled from the HF raw-completions bucket):

1. Oblique few-shot instructed context, probe "How does GPS calculate your location?" — clean factual answer, truncated at 256 tokens, NO marker. Consistent with the 0/400 oblique marker rate.
2. Pirate-captain context, back-pain probe — fully in-character reply ("Arrr, me hearty! ..."), truncated. No fishiness.
3. Helpful-assistant context, freedom/security probe — standard assistant prose, truncated.
4. Standard-template context, sound-propagation probe — standard prose, truncated.
5. Enumerated-rewrite context, well-lived-life probe — short bullet-list reply, ended naturally at 72 tokens (the panel's one short-responding context).

No fishiness: no sampling collapse (draws differ), no judge involved (no labels to disagree with), no empty outputs. One benign temp-1.0 code-switch token ("志愿服务") in one enumerated-rewrite reply — disclosed in the body. The dominant data feature is severe truncation (median context pair: 82% of samples hit the 256-token cap), which is treated as a load-bearing caveat in the interpretation.

### Background

Parent #532's leaderboard carried flagged methodology debt: its behavioral-divergence (JS) arm used the deprecated v1 estimator (single next-token distribution at the last input position). This run implements the canonical Rao-Blackwellized sequence-level JS (arXiv 2504.10637 §3; per-position full-vocab JS over R=8 temp-1.0 replies per side, base-2, length-normalized) and re-fits the JS arm on the identical 416-cell panel with the identical on-policy ※-emission DV.

### Methodology validation (all gates passed before interpretation)

- Reproduction control: ported parent phase-3 on unchanged v1 inputs reproduced parent numbers at tolerance 1e-9 (PASS).
- Empirical self-pair JS = 5.3e-9 bits (analytic zero).
- Position-0 RB values vs the v1 matrix: max |diff| 0.0070, mean 0.0012 across all 280 pairs (same mathematical object at the overlap position).
- Split-half reliability of js_rb (ordinary pairs): 0.998; median per-pair MC SE 0.0010 bits vs cross-pair spread 0.043 bits. The estimator is essentially noise-free at R=8 × 50 probes.

### Results claims

1. Ordinary strip (n=256): js_rb ρ = −0.486 (95% CI −0.573 to −0.385) vs js_v1 −0.410. Paired improvement +0.076 (cell-level 95% CI 0.030 to 0.125; clustered by unordered pair 0.023 to 0.139; LOCO jackknife −0.024 to 0.177 but all 16 per-context deltas positive). Plan taxonomy verdict: PARTIAL IMPROVEMENT (missed the ρ ≤ −0.50 confirmation bar). Gaussian KL stays the ordinary-strip leader at −0.620.
2. Union (n=416): js_rb ρ = −0.028 (permutation p = 0.584) vs v1 −0.350. Composition effect, not signal loss: instructed cells have higher mean js_rb (0.065 vs 0.050 bits/token) AND far higher emission (0.67 vs 0.10), so the between-strip contrast cancels the within-ordinary negative. v1's strip ordering was opposite (instructed 0.458 < ordinary 0.578 bits), so v1's union −0.35 was partly composition in the lucky direction. Hierarchy side: geometry-beyond-flag+prior CV-R² = 0.015 (js_rb) vs 0.054 (js_v1) vs 0.014 (gauss_kl) — union-level, same composition caveat.
3. Instructed strip (n=160): js_rb ρ = +0.139 (95% CI −0.031 to 0.287; p = 0.080) — indistinguishable from null given the variance; plan verdict CONFIRMED (|ρ| < 0.20). Marker-masked variant +0.137 (not ※ co-measurement). Residuals vs ordinary fit: explicit/soft contexts median +0.74 to +0.96 (138/160 above, p = 4.9e-22); obliques ≈ 0. The parent's "distance predictors stop carrying signal in instructed contexts; base prior is load-bearing" conclusion survives the estimator upgrade.
4. Length-nuisance check (plan-obligated): |Δ mean reply length| alone predicts emission at ρ = −0.537 (n=256) — nominally better than js_rb. Partial js_rb given length = −0.063 (p = 0.32, nothing left); partial length given js_rb = −0.233 (p = 0.0002). js_rb↔length ρ = 0.83. Gaussian KL survives the length control (−0.353, p = 6.3e-9) and subsumes the length feature (partial length given GKL = +0.02, p = 0.75). Robustness: excluding the diagonal AND the one short-responding context (Enumerated-framing rewrite; length-spread SD collapses to 6 tokens), length still beats js_rb (−0.373 vs −0.284, n=210) and length-partialled js_rb = 0.002 (p = 0.97). This is the headline: the canonical sequence-level JS tracks leakage no better than a response-length-difference feature.
5. Position profile: per-position divergence is front-loaded (~0.58 bits at position 0 for ordinary pairs, decaying to ~0.02 past position 100). The deprecated shortcut read the single most divergent position; estimator rank agreement ρ = 0.88 (ordinary off-diagonal). The canonical estimator's added information is the response tail, whose leakage-predictive content reduces to length structure per claim 4.

### Takeaways

- The methodology debt is closed; the parent's conclusions all survive (ordinary-strip direction preserved and modestly strengthened; instructed-strip collapse confirmed at the strongest available estimator).
- Pooled (union) correlations are composition-dominated for divergence predictors on this panel; only per-strip numbers are meaningful.
- Deflationary main finding: full-reply behavioral divergence carries no leakage-prediction signal beyond mean-reply-length divergence on this panel, while activation geometry (Gaussian KL@L22) carries strong length-free signal and subsumes the length feature. Predictor-program implication: prioritize activation geometry + base prior; deprioritize sequence-level behavioral divergence unless a length-diverse, higher-cap panel shows otherwise.

### Confidence rationale

MODERATE. Implementation validity is high (four independent validation gates passed). The deflationary length claim rests on a single panel whose length structure is censored by the 256-token cap (median 82% truncation) and dominated by one short-responding context — though the no-outlier subset robustness check (n=210, length SD 6 tokens) still shows length parity, the panel remains a weak test of what full-reply JS could measure with a larger cap. H2's CI is wide (upper bound 0.287 exceeds the 0.20 bar even though the point estimate is inside it).

### Next steps

- Re-measure canonical JS with a 1024-token cap on a length-diverse panel with a pre-specified length control (cost_class: needs-gpu, headline_affecting: yes).
- Add the length-difference feature as an explicit leaderboard column going forward (cost_class: free-analysis, headline_affecting: no).
